issues: db.py balanced_values (used by report_balance_sheet and report_trial_balance) quietly adds FX rounding differences to the largest account, so that account's reported value no longer matches its converted balance; also, ledger.report_ledger converts each posting at its own date, unlike the report-date rule other reports use.

db.select_postings loads every posting into Python and filters in memory, and it is called once per month in report_networth and once per budget via tree_total; txn_list, list_documents and report_aging also issue one query per row (N+1), so cost grows quickly as the book grows.

db.py mixes several unrelated jobs (schema, the command registry and argparse helpers, permissions, posting and FX logic, report valuation), and the layers leak: server.query_arguments has a special case for the 'payables' keyword, and errors.NotFound (documented as 'No such API route') is reused by docs.find_doc for a missing invoice.

There is duplicated or dead code: db.line_fields is unused and nearly identical to docs.parse_line; the mapping `"invoices" if kind == "invoice" else "bills"` is repeated in find_doc, pay_document, list_documents and report_aging; and import_cmd calls ensure_account again after category_for has already done so.

books.init runs executescript(SCHEMA) outside write_tx, so a failure before the meta and admin rows are committed leaves a half-built database that later init calls refuse; separately, period_close writes an audit entry even when closing an earlier month changes nothing.

The tests leave important edge cases uncovered: multi-currency reports and --currency, running recurring twice (idempotence), Jan 31 and Feb 29 recurrences through the CLI, duplicate rows within one import file, and the exact audit entry shapes; test_api also shares one server database across all tests, so the expected invoice numbering depends on which tests ran before.
strengths: Money is stored and calculated as integer cents, with Decimal used for rates and quantities and ROUND_HALF_UP rounding; fmt_cents guarantees two decimals and never prints -0.00, and all SQL values are passed as parameters.

The command registry (@command/@arguments plus db.call) puts permission checks, a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction with rollback, and audit logging in one place, and the CLI and HTTP API both use it, so behaviour and JSON shapes match.

Functions are small and well named, with clear docstrings; validation helpers (parse_date, parse_cents, clean_text, check_open) are used the same way everywhere, and user errors map cleanly to exit code 2 or the right HTTP status.
